title: Chelex DNA Extraction Protocol
author: Sarah Chang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.byvhpw36
materials: Cover plate and incubate in the thermocycler under the following conditions: 60°C for 120 min (tissue digestion) 95°C for 15 min (heat kill for proteinase K) This protocol should be saved in most of the thermocyclers (just scroll through). Sometimes this is not sufficient for complete digestion, so a second addition of 5uL of proteinase K followed by a repeat of the incubation procedure may be necessary. Alternatively, you could increase the digestion period from 120 min to 240 min. This is what I usually do and seems to work quite well.

steps.title: Prepare 10% Chelex solution
steps.instruction: Make enough 10% Chelex for the entire 96‑well plate (195 µL per well plus extra). Dissolve 1 g Chelex resin in 9 mL deionized water to obtain a 10 % (w/v) solution.

steps.title: Stir Chelex solution continuously
steps.instruction: Place a magnetic stir bar in the jar containing the 10 % Chelex solution and keep it stirring to maintain a uniform suspension, as Chelex powder is very heavy.

steps.title: Dispense Chelex into plate wells
steps.instruction: Pipette 195 µL of the 10 % Chelex solution into each well of a 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Add tissue sample to each well
steps.instruction: Add an approximately 1 mm² piece of tissue (e.g., operculum punch or adipose fin clip) to each well. Handle carefully to avoid disturbing the Chelex volume.

steps.title: Add proteinase K to each well
steps.instruction: Using a repeater pipette, add 5 µL of proteinase K to each well. This must be the final addition, because proteinase K will self‑digest at room temperature without substrate.

substeps.instruction: Vortex briefly to break up any remaining tissue fragments.
Vortex at 1500 rpm for 2 minutes to collect Chelex and other solids at the bottom of the well.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new plate
steps.instruction: Pipette off the clear supernatant from each well and dispense it into a new 96‑well plate; this is the undiluted DNA stock. Store the stock at –20 °C in chimney‑well plates with caps.

steps.title: Create 1:10 dilution plate
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:10 dilution plate for downstream assays (typically 200 µL total per well) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Add 180 µL deionized water to each well.
Add 20 µL of the undiluted DNA stock to each well.
Vortex the plate and briefly spin down the contents.
Store the dilution plate in the refrigerator to avoid multiple freeze‑thaw cycles.
